title: Introduction to C++
html:
A compiled, statically typed, multi-paradigm language that gives you C-level control of memory with high-level abstractions that cost nothing at run time.

C++ — a general-purpose language created by Bjarne Stroustrup (1979, “C with Classes”). Source is compiled ahead of time to native machine code — no virtual machine, no garbage collector.

Why C++?

Performance

Compiles to native code; you decide where every object lives (stack, heap, static). Used where latency matters: games, trading, browsers, databases.

Zero-overhead abstractions

“What you don't use, you don't pay for; what you do use, you couldn't hand-code better.” Templates and inlining make std::sort as fast as hand-written C.

Multi-paradigm

Procedural (like C), object-oriented (classes, virtual functions), generic (templates) and functional (lambdas, ranges) — mix as needed.

Deterministic cleanup

Destructors run at a known point (end of scope) — the basis of RAII, C++'s answer to resource management.

C vs C++

FeatureCC++
ParadigmProceduralProcedural + OOP + generic + functional
StructsData onlyclass/struct with methods, access control, inheritance
Memorymalloc / freenew / delete, but prefer containers & smart pointers
Stringschar* + <string.h>std::string, std::string_view
Pass byValue or pointerValue, pointer or reference (int&)
OverloadingNoFunction & operator overloading
Generic codeMacros / void*Templates, concepts
ErrorsReturn codes, errnoExceptions (plus return codes, std::optional)
NamespacesNo (one global scope)namespace
Standard librarySmall (stdio, stdlib…)STL: containers, algorithms, threads, chrono, …
Compatibility

C++ is almost a superset of C — most C compiles as C++, but not all (e.g. int *p = malloc(4); needs a cast in C++, and class/new are keywords).

Your first program

The standards

StandardHeadline features
C++98/03STL, templates, exceptions, std::string
C++11The “modern C++” reset: auto, lambdas, move semantics, nullptr, smart pointers, range-for, constexpr, threads
C++14Generic lambdas, make_unique, relaxed constexpr
C++17Structured bindings, optional/variant/any, string_view, if constexpr, filesystem
C++20Concepts, ranges, coroutines, modules, <=>, std::format, std::span
C++23std::print, std::expected, ranges::to, deducing this
Version

These notes use C++20 (every example is compiled with clang++ -std=c++20). C++23 features are mentioned where relevant.

Is C++ an object-oriented language?

It supports OOP but doesn't force it. It's multi-paradigm: you can write procedural code, generic code with templates, or functional-style code with lambdas and ranges. A C++ program doesn't need a single class.

Why is C++ faster than Java or Python?

It compiles straight to native code with aggressive optimisation (inlining, templates specialised per type), has no garbage-collector pauses and no interpreter/JIT warm-up, and lets you control memory layout (contiguous std::vector, objects on the stack). The trade-off is that memory safety is your responsibility.
